tagline.text: A small island of sea turtles and black marble northwest of Romblon

location.label: Location
location.text: Cobrador Barangay (formerly Naguso), Romblon Municipality, Romblon Province

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500~3,500 (boat charter and local costs, per group)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Tugdan Airport (TBH, Tablas Island), or travel via the Kalibo/Caticlan side

children.text: Cobrador Island is a small island village northwest of Romblon Island, formerly called Naguso. It is known for fine white sand, coral waters, a hidden natural swimming pool called Tinagong Dagat, and black marble. It is about 1 hour by boat from Romblon town, so an island-hopping day trip is possible when the weather cooperates.

Cobrador Island is a small island barangay belonging to Romblon municipality in the Romblon island group. Together with Alad Island and Logbon Island, which belong to the same municipality, it lies scattered in the sea northwest of Romblon Island. The village was formerly called Naguso (or Nagoso) and was renamed Cobrador in 1960. According to the 2020 census it has about 880 residents, so it is a quiet fishing village rather than a tourist destination.

The island was once known as a source of black marble. Romblon is the center of the Philippine marble industry, and Cobrador is famous for its black stone. For travelers, though, the sea is a bigger draw than the rock. The wide white-sand beach and clear water on the western side near Cabugaan, the coral zone offshore, the natural swimming pool at the northern tip called Tinagong Dagat, and the caves and rock formations inside the island are the signature sights.

Sea turtles are said to visit this island, and there are reports that the village works with the local government and environmental groups to protect their habitat and nesting sites. A small environmental fee is reportedly collected for this reason, so even in turtle season, the basic etiquette is not to touch or chase turtles and to keep your distance.

The journey is not easy. From Manila you travel overnight by ferry to Romblon town, then take a small bangka (boat) for about 30 minutes to 1 hour (guides differ). About half of the sea crossing is open water, where the waves are often rough. This makes it a good island for travelers who leave slack in their schedule and move according to the weather. For first-time visitors, here is what I recommend: stay 1–2 nights in Romblon town, do a hop through Cobrador, Alad and Logbon in one day when the sea is good, and spend the remaining days around Romblon town and its marble workshops. Think of it as a quick visit to a quiet island village rather than a long resort stay, and your expectations will match reality.

On the western side near Cabugaan there is a wide white-sand beach with clear water. It is the easiest spot for swimming and relaxing. There is coral offshore, so it pairs well with snorkeling. There is almost no shade or parasols, so bring a hat and a towel, and when the tide is out the coral side gets shallow, so watch where you step.
A natural saltwater pool at the northern tip of the island, described as a pool about
2 m
deep surrounded by rock. The name means "hidden sea." When the waves are high the boat cannot land, so some visitors leave without seeing it.

In the shallow, clear water you can see coral and tropical fish. Even if you are not a confident swimmer you can enjoy it close to shore. Check life jackets and gear locally in advance. The water looks clearest in the morning when the sun is not yet high. Do not swim far from shore, and always stay within sight of the boat.

The Wikipedia entry for Romblon municipality describes it as the largest natural cave in the island group. There is a description that it was considered an ancient burial ground. Treat it with care, follow the guidance of local residents, and look around quietly.
Climbing Mt. Baco in the island's interior is reported to give 360-degree views of the island and the surrounding sea. The island's highest point is known to be about

, so it is not a long hike. Ask in the village about the condition of the trail. Sneakers or trekking sandals are safer than flip-flops, and it is best to ask a local for the way before you set out. Avoid the hot midday sun.

blocks.title: A village that protects turtle habitat

children.text: It is known as a place where sea turtles feed and nest, and there are reports that the village leads their protection. You might be lucky enough to see one, or you might not. If you do, watch quietly from a distance.

Cobrador is known as an island where black marble is found. Seen together with the marble workshops on Romblon Island, it makes the story of the local industry easier to understand. If you stop at a marble workshop or shop in Romblon town, you can get closer to the stone story of this area.

items.title: Island-hopping day trip
items.subtitle: Leaving in the morning from Romblon town

children.text: Board a bangka at Romblon town port. On days with rough waves, be sure to ask the boatman about sea conditions before departing.
Leave the port and arrive at Cobrador's western shore after about
30 minutes–1 hour
Swim and snorkel at the beach. The coral zone is shallow, so when playing where you can touch the bottom, take care not to step on the coral.
If the sea allows, move by boat to Tinagong Dagat at the northern end of the island. If the waves are high, skip it and go around the coast.
Have the packed lunch you brought, or rent a hut on Alad Island and order local food.
Stop at the next island (Alad or Logbon) or return to Romblon town. Plan to be back before sunset at the latest.
The boat charter is priced as one trip out. A full-day tour combining Alad and Logbon is more common than going to Cobrador alone.
Buy groceries and water in Romblon town and board the boat. Many things are hard to get on the island.
Drop your bags at a beachfront cottage or village lodging. According to reports there are a few simple beachside cottages, so contact them in advance to check.
Enjoy a quiet beach walk and the sunset.
Do a Mt. Baco trek or a village walk in the morning, then return to Romblon town.
There are few rooms and almost no official information, so be sure to check cottage availability locally.
From Manila, take a bus to Batangas Port (or Lucena Port). An intercity bus takes about
2–3 hours

From Batangas Port, an overnight Starlite ferry to Romblon town (departing around 4 PM, arriving the next early morning) is listed. The fare per the June 2025 schedule is ₱1,800~2,500 (seat to cabin, terminal fees extra), and sailings can be cancelled or changed, so confirm with the operator. From Lucena (Montenegro or StarHorse, departing 3–4 PM), you reach Romblon in the early morning via San Agustin on Tablas Island.
From Lucena Port, Montenegro or StarHorse depart in the afternoon and reach Romblon town via San Agustin in the early morning.
Ferry days and times change often and cancellations due to weather are frequent. Check directly with the operator before departing.

After arriving in Romblon town, you can start arranging a boat charter to Cobrador at your lodging or near the port pier. Overnight boats often arrive in the early morning, so plan the first day as a rest day.
I could not confirm a direct flight from Manila to Romblon. There are reports of limited flights to Tugdan Airport on Tablas Island, but check the latest schedule.
Find an island-hopping boat at the Romblon town port pier, or ask a resort to arrange a charter.
Travel time is listed as about
30 minutes–1 hour
depending on the weather. Allow around 45 minutes as a rule.
I could not confirm whether there is a regular passenger boat. Assume a chartered boat is the norm.
Romblon is said to have no distinct wet and dry seasons, and the annual mean temperature is about
. Annual rainfall is reported at about 2,378 mm.

Waves are the biggest variable for boats to the island. March–May, when the sea is calm, is the most stable, and cancellations are frequent in typhoon season, so leave at least one extra day in your schedule.
On island-hopping days the wind is relatively weak in the morning and waves often grow in the afternoon, so it is best to leave as early as possible and return in the early afternoon.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
Cobrador has no resort facilities, and a few simple beachside cottages are reported. A figure of about
per night is listed, but the number of cottages is limited, so contact them in advance to confirm availability. Most travelers stay in lodging in Romblon town and visit as a day trip.
It is safest to prepare food in Romblon town. It is reported that on Alad Island you can rent a hut and order lunch. Bring your own water, snacks and a trash bag, and take your trash back with you.

Romblon town has small, long-established lodgings and eateries clustered around the port, so arriving a day early, staying one night and leaving early in the morning is the easy way to do it. If you agree on the departure time, charter fee and return time with the boatman the evening before, you reduce arguments on the day. It is convenient to ask a shop near the port in advance to prepare a packed lunch.
Before departing, be sure to ask a local or your lodging in Romblon town about wave conditions. About half of the sea crossing is open water.
You can ask a resort to arrange a boat or find one directly at the port pier. Agree on the price first and decide whether to include Alad and Logbon in the route.
Bring a waterproof bag, sandals, sunscreen, a hat and spare clothes. Getting splashed on the boat is common.
Bring plenty of cash. It is safest to assume there is no ATM on the island.
When snorkeling, do not step on or touch the coral. If you see a turtle, keep your distance and take photos without flash.
Tinagong Dagat can only be entered in good weather. Even if you miss it, do not be disappointed and enjoy the beach instead.
Mobile signal is weak, so download maps and your itinerary in advance.
The day before departure, agree on the departure and return times and the total price with the boatman. It is safer to set the return time before sunset.
Waves on the sea crossing are often rough, so cancellations and failed landings are common. Leave at least one extra day for the return boat and your flight home.
Boat fares are negotiated and there is no firm rate table, so confirm the total before departing.
It is safest to assume there is no medical facility on the island, so bring basic medicine.
Lodging, environmental fee and peak-season rules can change, so check the latest announcements.
Because this is a little-documented island, blogs differ in their descriptions of its location and area. Check once more locally.
Always wear a life jacket, and do not push your luck on days with high waves.
Caves and remote shores are not close to rescue services, so do not go deep in alone and move together with local villagers.
The main island that serves as the starting point. It has marble workshops and Spanish-era sites, and you find boats to Cobrador from its port.
Island barangays of the same Romblon municipality, usually combined with Cobrador in a one-day hopping route. Alad is reported to have coral and marine sanctuaries.
A small island in the Romblon island group, good for enjoying a quiet sea.
A large island in the Romblon group with big mountains and waterfalls, suited to trekking and nature trips.
